title: Jill Watson: A Virtual Teaching Assistant for Online Education
supports_claim: The Georgia Tech technical report states that Jill Watson operated in the OMSCS 7637 Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence discussion forums from Spring 2016; about 750 students had interacted with versions of the system, and the Spring 2017 version autonomously handled introductions, announcements, and routine frequently asked questions.
limitations: The repository metadata gives only the publication year 2016; this is a first-party technical report rather than an independent peer-reviewed evaluation, and it does not establish learning gains, long-term effects, or reliability for generative explanations of AI concepts.

title: CodeHelp: Using Large Language Models with Guardrails for Scalable Support in Programming Classes
supports_claim: The Koli Calling 2023 paper reports a 12-week deployment with 52 students in a first-year computer and data science course; CodeHelp used guardrails intended to provide guidance without directly revealing solutions and to complement instructor and teaching-assistant support.
limitations: This was a small single-course deployment; survey participation was optional and incentivized, the instructor was also an author, and the study did not establish causal learning gains or reliability for every AI-course topic.

title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
supports_claim: Seven evaluated GPT detectors misclassified human-written TOEFL essays by non-native English writers at a much higher rate than the comparison set of US eighth-grade essays.
limitations: The study used 91 TOEFL essays, 88 US eighth-grade essays, and a specific set of detectors available in 2023; it did not evaluate every detector or an AI tutor.

title: Guidance on AI Detection and Why We're Disabling Turnitin's AI Detector
supports_claim: Vanderbilt reported disabling Turnitin's AI detection feature after reviewing reliability, transparency, false-positive, bias, and student-data privacy concerns.
limitations: This is a first-party institutional decision rather than an independent technical audit; its 750-paper illustration extrapolates a vendor-claimed 1% false-positive rate and is not an observed incident count.

title: Law 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: Vietnam's official legal portal records the Artificial Intelligence Law as effective from 1 March 2026 and establishes the primary legal instrument that must be assessed for the pilot.
limitations: The official metadata confirms the instrument and effective date, but the exact duties depend on the final intended purpose, system role, workflow, and facts of deployment.

title: Decree 142/2026/ND-CP detailing implementation of the Artificial Intelligence Law
supports_claim: Vietnam's official legal portal records Decree 142/2026/ND-CP as effective from 1 May 2026 and as detailing measures for implementation of the Artificial Intelligence Law.
limitations: Applicability cannot be inferred from the decree title alone; qualified review must map the complete product purpose, provider and deployer roles, data flow, and controls to the signed text.

title: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg issuing the list of high-risk artificial intelligence systems
supports_claim: Vietnam's official legal portal records Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg and its high-risk AI system list as effective from 15 August 2026.
limitations: A legal reviewer must compare AIGuide's exact intended purpose and excluded grading, disciplinary, deployment, and external-action functions with the complete signed list; the source title alone does not determine classification.

title: Law 91/2025/QH15 on Personal Data Protection
supports_claim: Vietnam's official legal portal records the Personal Data Protection Law as effective from 1 January 2026, making student interaction and vendor data flows subject to a dedicated privacy applicability review.
limitations: The portal metadata does not by itself determine lawful basis, data roles, retention, cross-border transfer, or whether a particular pilot field is sensitive personal data.

title: EU AI Act policy framework and implementation timeline
supports_claim: The Commission states that chatbot transparency rules apply from August 2026 and that Annex III high-risk rules for specified education uses apply from 2 December 2027.
limitations: The current pilot targets Vietnam only, and any future EU classification would still depend on intended purpose, provider or deployer role, affected people, and whether the system evaluates outcomes or steers learning in a listed way.
